_: The three doors: the site arranged by what a visitor came to do, rather than by which repository a page came from. Membership only; every title and description is read from lib/pages.ts, the manifest, a tool's own page or the docs tree, so a page is named in one place. A group's name and line are the one thing written here, because a grouping exists nowhere else; a door that wants none has a single group with no name. A path may sit behind two doors (a tool is both a thing to watch and a thing to build on) and that is the point: a door is a way in, not a folder.
measured: Which pages exist, how many doors lead to each, how long each one is and how many links it offers are measured by scripts/crawl-site.py and shown at /style/map. The doors print the length and the links beside each page from that same record.

doors.name: Watch it run
doors.what: The machines, running in the page. Nothing here is a recording: every frame, every trace and every byte is computed while you look at it, on models built from the chips' own transistors.

doors.name: Read how it was done
doors.what: The story and the record: the arc of the work told once from the start, the long reads, the notebook of plans and reports, and where each project introduces itself.

groups.name: The arc
groups.what: How the console came to work, told once from the start. Begin here if you have read none of it.

groups.name: The long reads
groups.what: Each instrument's prose lifted out from under it and set as an article, justified and written to be read end to end.

groups.name: The notebook
groups.what: Every plan written before the work and every report written after it, with the figures they were written from. These are lists: pick an axis and open what it points at.

groups.name: The two projects
groups.what: Where the console and the chip each introduce themselves, with the lesson and the recovered visual6502 wiki.

doors.name: Build on it
doors.what: The parts you can use: a chip that answers over HTTP, a cartridge format, a registry that re-runs what it publishes, and the bytes from a real Geiger tube.
